claims.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
claims.evidence: For fixed labeled bugs and hosts, a vertex v can receive exactly the nonempty subsets of A(v), the bugs hosted in N[v]. Thus feasible pairwise-distinct signatures are exactly a matching saturating all vertices in the bipartite graph described. In either direction, the matching immediately defines valid monitoring zones. Enumerating all host multisets for every t≤k and testing matching takes f(k)n^{k+O(1)} time.
claims.witness: Given a saturating matching, assign each vertex its matched subset and define M(b)={v:b belongs to the matched subset of v}; conversely, the signatures of any fixed-placement solution are matching edges.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the equivalence directly from the source definition, then checked the matching implementation against every greedy prefix used by the finite constructions.

claims.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
claims.evidence: Every code of a vertex in X is a distinct nonempty subset of the bugs hosted in N[X]. With h such bugs there are only 2^h−1 possible codes, so h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). A bug cannot monitor across components; restricting a solution gives component solutions, while the union of component solutions remains identifying because nonempty codes over disjoint bug sets cannot coincide.
claims.witness: For additivity, relabel componentwise bug sets disjointly and unite optimal component systems; this attains the sum matching the restriction lower bound.
claims.search_method: Direct counting and both directions of the component decomposition were checked from the monitoring-zone definition.

claims.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Applying claim 1 to X=C gives the lower bound. If u is universal in C, h=ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs hosted at u are available to every vertex, and |C| distinct nonempty subsets exist. This realizes the bound. Component summation and finding universal vertices are polynomial-time operations.
claims.witness: Host h bugs at a universal vertex and assign any |C| distinct masks among 1,…,2^h−1.
claims.search_method: Checked the information lower bound and supplied the matching explicit construction component by component.

claims.claim: Let G be formed from a clique C={c_1,…,c_s} by attaching a_i pendant vertices adjacent only to c_i. Then OPT(G)=max{ceil(log2(|V(G)|+1)), sum_i ceil(log2(a_i+1))}; the optimum and a witnessing surveillance system are constructible in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Moving a leaf-hosted bug to its center preserves its old zone because N[leaf]⊆N[center]. Thereafter the a_i private leaves can use only the p_i bugs at c_i, forcing p_i≥ceil(log2(a_i+1)); global code counting gives the other lower bound. For K equal to the displayed maximum, allocate disjoint groups P_i totaling K and meeting these minima. Private leaves receive distinct nonempty P_i-subsets. These codes are mutually distinct across groups, and at least s unused nonempty K-bit subsets remain for the clique vertices, which hear every bug. The allocation and mask scan are polynomial.
claims.witness: The constructive witness consists of groups P_i hosted at c_i, distinct nonempty local masks for its leaves, and any s unused global masks for the clique vertices.
claims.search_method: Proved both lower bounds and the general construction; additionally exhaustively solved 39 small clique-pendant graphs with exact matching.

claims.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
claims.evidence: Double counting gives sum_v |S(v)|=sum_b |M(b)|≤k rho. The n codes are distinct nonempty k-subsets, so their total size is at least L(n,k). Filling subset-size layers from cardinality one upward yields the stated closed formula; at most k codes can be singletons, implying L(n,k)≥2n−k.
claims.witness: The extremal family defining L consists of all subsets of sizes below s and the required number of size-s subsets, where s is the first layer whose cumulative count reaches n.
claims.search_method: Performed the incidence double count symbolically and exactly enumerated all subset-size layers for k=1,…,7.

claims.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
claims.evidence: A connected maximum-degree-two graph is a path or cycle, and an interval graph has no induced cycle of length at least four, leaving paths and K3. K3 has optimum two by the universal-vertex formula. For P_n, incidence capacity gives k≥ceil(n/2). If n=2t and k=t, equality forces t singleton and t pair codes and forces every bug to occupy an internal vertex and monitor all three vertices of its closed neighborhood. Equal or adjacent hosts then create duplicate pair codes, so hosts must be distinct nonadjacent internal vertices; P_{2t} has at most t−1 such vertices, a contradiction. Alternating odd-position hosts construct the claimed optimum for odd paths; the even construction adds one bug at the final vertex.
claims.witness: For P_{2t+1}, bugs at 1,3,…,2t+1 give singleton codes to odd vertices and adjacent-bug pairs to even vertices. For P_{2t}, use bugs at 1,3,…,2t−1 plus one at 2t.
claims.search_method: Checked the graph classification, completed the even-path equality case, and exhaustively computed exact optima for P_1 through P_10 and K3.

claims.claim: The unmodified source Surveillance algorithm has worst-case approximation ratio at least 4/3, even on connected interval families.
claims.evidence: The six intervals are in source timeline order and have q=(2,3,5,6,6,6). Exact execution adds at (process,host)=(1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,6). Before the last addition, the availability masks collectively offer only five distinct nonempty signatures to six vertices. Three bugs at J2,J3,J4 support the six stated distinct codes, while six vertices require at least ceil(log2(7))=3 bugs. Hence OPT=3 and the source algorithm uses four. The intersection graph is connected.
claims.search_method: Reproduced ComputeSignatures using the source lexicographic rule and independently cross-checked every prefix by exact bipartite matching.

claims.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
claims.evidence: Exact rational ordering produces the claimed forward order and additions (1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13). Reflecting the entire family produces the same interval set, so the opposite-direction execution has the same seven additions. The supplied six-host signature assignment is feasible and pairwise distinct. Moreover, N[{L1,…,L4}]={L1,…,L6} and the reflected region has neighborhood {R1,…,R6}; these host regions are disjoint and each four-vertex set forces three bugs. Thus OPT≥6, matching the witness.
claims.witness: Host a,b,c at L2,L3,L5 and d,e,f at R5,R3,R2; use the six left codes and their reflected right codes from the draft, with U assigned {c,d}.
claims.search_method: Computed all intersections and both source-algorithm executions with exact fractions, validated the signature witness, and exactly checked the two neighborhood unions.

claims.claim: The algorithmic obstructions amplify without dilution: for every r≥1 there is a 6r-interval family on which the source algorithm uses 4r bugs while OPT=3r, and a 13r-interval family on which both timeline directions use 7r bugs while OPT=6r.
claims.evidence: Translate r copies far enough apart that they form separate components ordered consecutively. Bugs in previous components are unavailable in the current component, and nonempty codes over disjoint component bug sets never collide, so every local greedy addition trace is unchanged and costs add. Reversing direction only reverses component order and invokes the corresponding local reverse trace. Claim 1 makes OPT additive, yielding exactly 4r versus 3r and 7r versus 6r.
claims.witness: Use separated translates of the verified six-interval obstruction for the first family and separated translates of the reflection-symmetric thirteen-interval obstruction for the second.
claims.search_method: Verified both base traces exactly, then proved preservation of feasibility decisions, algorithm costs, and optimum under separated disjoint union.

claims.claim: The decision problem parameterized by the bug budget k is fixed-parameter tractable: OPT≤k can be decided in 2^{O(k^2)} times a polynomial in the input size.
claims.evidence: A YES-instance has n≤2^k−1 because k bugs provide at most that many nonempty codes. After rejecting larger instances, for each t≤k there are at most n^t≤(2^k−1)^k=2^{O(k^2)} labeled placements. Claim 0 tests each placement using at most 2^t−1 right-side signature vertices, adding only 2^{O(k)} polynomial work. Summing over t preserves the stated FPT bound.
claims.witness: The algorithm rejects when n>2^k−1; otherwise it enumerates all t-bug host maps for 0≤t≤k and accepts exactly when one fixed-placement matching saturates V.
claims.search_method: Derived the size bound, placement count, matching-instance size, and total parameter dependence independently.

target_evidence: All ten bound claims survive, but none proves either branch of the exact source target. Exact restricted subclasses and an FPT decision algorithm do not give an unrestricted polynomial-time approximation below 2. Ratios 4/3 and 7/6 are lower bounds only for the specified greedy procedures, not inapproximability bounds for the problem. The draft explicitly says the general threshold remains unresolved and labels itself PARTIAL, which accurately describes material but incomplete progress.
